newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent slashes gains, downtrend silences APIs.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent slashes gains, downtrend silences APIs.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures fell quickly from session highs to session lows as an imposing two-month downtrend failed to be deterred by U.S. inventory data that many traders said was constructive for products markets.

A swift selloff in world financial markets after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan voiced concern about soaring stock prices and the risk of higher inflation, may have dragged oil prices lower in sympathy, some brokers said. Others said it was only coincidental.
At 1605 GMT, April Brent traded three cents higher at $19.48 a barrel after hitting a session low of $19.30.
Minutes earlier, it jumped to a session high of $19.84 when NYMEX oil futures opened sharply higher.
March gas oil tripped even more, trading $2.25 lower at $166.50 a tonne. It hit a session low of $165, near its eight-month low of $163.50 that was registered on Tuesday.
"It could be a little bit of spillover from the financial markets," said one oil broker. "I can't put it down to anything other than that. The APIs were rather friendly."
American Petroleum Institute and the Energy Information Administration showed a drop in gasoline and distillate inventories for last week.
The EIA also reported a small drop in crude supplies.
"Certainly, people aren't convinced (by the APIs) and are more convinced in the overriding technical picture," an analyst said.

The expiry of the March NYMEX products on Friday and Brent crude's ability to hold support at $19 a barrel earlier this week, after a drop of 20 percent since early January, has boosted volatility and clouded the near-term picture, brokers said.
